chunks.title: [Henan University of Engineering x CLO] Underbust with segmented princess seams
chunks.content: ## Underbust Style with Segmented Princess Seams This section explains the characteristics and handling of an underbust style featuring a division line at the lower part of the chest, often involving segmented princess seams. Key terms include A-spleen, B-spleen, division line, and arch transfer. The style examined is characterized by a division passing through the lower chest area, often with the chest turned or cut. Unlike the round shape, the A-spleen is removed, and the B-spleen is eliminated or transferred to create a flat lower chest surface. The thoracic spine fold disappears, replaced by more folds at the lower chest division line. When a division line passes through both the A-spleen and B-spleen areas, the A-spleen is temporarily transferred out, and the B-spleen is eliminated to flatten the lower chest. This flattening facilitates drawing the division line, which is then adjusted in a 3D window for accuracy. The process starts by analyzing and measuring the structure, including identifying key points like the BP point. A flat contour line below the chest is ideal for drawing the separation line, which is typically positioned about 1.8 cm below the BP point. This distance corresponds to the lower chest measurement. The front edge and side seam are drawn according to style chart proportions. After drawing the separation line, the piece below it is cut off without further changes, while the upper section requires modification due to the absence of an arch. The arch is transferred to the new position using the arch transfer method, involving selecting the arch edge, rotating it, and positioning it closer to the BP point. The arch's fold amount, rather than the arch amount itself, is adjusted and merged into the new position to maintain smoothness. Following arch transfer, smoothing tools are used to eliminate irregularities, ensuring a natural curve. Excess lines from the drawing process are deleted for cleanliness. ## Arch Transfer and Seamline Adjustment This section details the arch transfer technique and seamline merging to maintain smooth and accurate garment shaping when working with segmented princess seams. The arch transfer is performed by holding the Shift key to select the arch edge and rotating it with the mouse. The arch is repositioned closer to the BP point and merged carefully, focusing on the fold amount rather than the arch amount. The original arch edge is deleted after merging. After transfer, the new seamline often is not smooth, requiring the use of an editor's far-fetched tool to smooth the curve. This ensures the arch and seamline blend naturally. For merging seamlines, converting points to free-line points is essential. Directly merging top and bottom points evenly distributes excess value, but in practice, the distribution is concentrated in the main seam area rather than evenly spread. The front and middle points maintain equal spacing, with the excess fold amount concentrated where needed. Opening the pattern in the 3D window and arranging points allows for better visualization and printing preparation. Printing holds the pattern's amount stable, temporarily removing folds from view.

Directly merging top and bottom points evenly distributes excess value, but in practice, the distribution is concentrated in the main seam area rather than evenly spread. The front and middle points maintain equal spacing, with the excess fold amount concentrated where needed. Opening the pattern in the 3D window and arranging points allows for better visualization and printing preparation. Printing holds the pattern's amount stable, temporarily removing folds from view. ## Fold Creation and Adjustment in 3D This section covers creating decorative folds using 3D software tools, including fold cutting, edge curve adjustment, and quality enhancement to match design intent. If the fold effect is insufficient after merging and printing, additional fold creation is necessary through 3D cutting functions. Starting from the shoulder line and dragging to the fold start point opens the lower chest area, adding decorative folds. The edge curve tool is used to adjust folds for smoothness and levelness by right-clicking to view and modify the fold line. Shoulder lines require adjustment as well since cutting alters their straightness. Shape-to-fold curve adjustments convert points and lines into free-line points for better control. This ensures folds focus on the chest area without unintended deformation in other areas, keeping front and side measurements consistent. Continuous checking confirms that folds are larger and closer to the intended style effect. Increasing the rendering quality in the 3D window provides a closer approximation to the final design appearance. --- This structured approach ensures precise handling of underbust styles with segmented princess seams, enabling accurate drafting, arch transfer, and fold creation for garment construction.
